newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses claw back losses, dlr stronger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses claw back losses, dlr stronger.

text.p: European bourses on Monday regained a little confidence and clawed back some of the steep early losses triggered by Wall Street's two percent drop on Friday.

On currency markets, the dollar climbed strongly against the mark and yen, rebounding from Friday's dramatic fall. Sterling also recovered somewhat but traders said the markets was still jittery ahead of UK inflation data late this week.

London, Frankfurt and Paris stocks all tumbled by about one percent at the opening before regaining some compusure in late morning. They had been badly rattled by New York's fall by 156.78 points to 8,031.22 on Friday.
The European bourses had already suffered substantial losses on Friday because falling New York stock prices sparked fears that the bull run on both sides of the Atlantic was slowing.
London's FTSE 100 began down 64.9 points down at 4,966.4 but, helped by benign inflation data and a shortage of stock, managed to climb back above the 5,000-point milestone only recently reached.

The market's recovery started with factory gate price figures seen as showing dormant inflation pressures. "There's nothing specific in the figures to help the market recover but overall they were reasonable," said SBC Warburg strategist George Hodgson.
But investors were growing increasingly edgy about whether the surge in London blue-chip shares, up 33 percent in the last year, had finally run out of steam.
"The market's nervous about whether it's peaked and despite the drop on Friday, the FTSE (100) was up about 130 points on the week so thing's look rather vulnerable," said another dealer.

In Frankfurt, stocks opened down about one percent but recovered some ground by late morning. "The sell-off this morning was on the back of Wall Street and the dollar, but it has been squeezing back since that. Not exactly a huge correction," a Frankfurt broker said.
Paris too bounced back from its early losses but was still down 0.5 percent. "It's relatively calm, it's not a huge sell-off," equity salesman John Fordyce at Oddo said.

In currency markets, the dollar gathered momentum on the mark and the yen by midday, correcting some of Friday's fall when it plunged four pfennigs and over four yen in sympathy with the decline in U.S. asset markets.

The U.S. currency clilmbed more than one pfennig to 1.8575 marks and half a yen to 115.73 and dealers said the dollar outlook was good, with U.S. economic fundamentals outshining those of Germany and Japan.

The summer holiday period has reduced the number of players in the market and increased volatility. "Nervousness will continue even though at this stage people are more inclined to be buyers than sellers," said Chris Furness, foreign exchange strategist at 4Cast Ltd in London.
The sharp decline of the dollar last week was in part triggered by speculation that the Bundesbank might nudge the repurchase rate higher from 3.00 percent at Tuesday's repo tender.

The sell-off accelerated late in Europe on Friday after Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing was quoted in a newspaper as saying German price developments were moving in the wrong direction in all areas, including consumer prices.

The British pound rebounded four pfennigs to 2.9580 marks and was up three cents to $1.5936 from Friday's dramatic falls. Sterling has been badly hit by official signals that British interest rates had peaked for the time being.
"There was something of an over-reaction last week in a thin market," Stewart Newnham, International Economist at First Chicago, said.

Sterling reached an eight-year peak of 3.0878 marks last month, when most analysts felt it was overvalued, and traders said the market was sitting on its hands ahead of a sensitive U.K. data late this week

But some remained upbeat. Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist for Europe at Bank of America, said: The pound is pretty much at a bottom now. Over the next few months we could be looking at a move up towards three marks again."
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.8575 marks and 115.73 yen, compared with 1.8453 and 115.12 in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 4.7 points at 5,026.6.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was 21.02 points down at 4,333.13 in bourse floor trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was down 15.74 points at 2,980.53.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $326.20 an ounce in the morning, up from Friday's London close of $325.05. Silver was at $4.40, down a cent.
